description: AGSC-01-22 as amended at rc.6 (D113): import tolerance has one limit and one record. Derivation, case by case. (1) `newer-source-refused`: the source declares `spec_version: 1.1.0`, a MINOR this 1.0 tool does not implement. AGSC-00-21 lists the constructs a 1.x reader can safely ignore in a document it did not author, and a whole unimplemented MINOR is not one of them — so the import stops before writing anything, with AGSC-E004, the code AGSC-00-20 already uses for a configuration value of a version a tool does not claim. It is exit 2 and not exit 1, because AGSC-09-08 puts invalid configuration in the usage class; no file is written, and `--dry-run` reports the same thing. (2) `allow-newer-writes`: the same source with the adapter's own `--allow-newer` flag — an adapter-scoped flag under AGSC-01-26a, which AGSC-09-09 already admits without a change to its closed list — is imported, and the operator, not the tool, has taken the risk. Each written item carries `prov.source_version` and `prov.source_hash`, taken verbatim from the source's published content version and bundle hash, and `prov.origin` stays `imported` as AGSC-01-31 and AGSC-08-01 already require. (3) `source-states-neither`: a source that publishes no content version and no bundle hash — a Level-0 publisher, AGSC-06-08a — yields items with both members absent; neither is ever invented, because a value nobody published cannot be recorded as if somebody had.
note: added 2026-09-22 at rc.6 (EXT-1); expected values derived by hand from the rule text, not from a run of any engine
